rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must not imitate Jews who claimed to accept their messenger while failing to do so.
rows.anchor: not follow the ways of the Jews who would claim before their messenger that they accepted when, in fact, they had not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥammad invites people to true life, and they should follow his invitation wholeheartedly.
rows.anchor: Muḥammad (sws) is inviting them to true life. They should whole-heartedly follow it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who refuse the Messenger after hearing and understanding his preaching face God's law intervening between them and their hearts, which are then sealed forever.
rows.anchor: Those who do not open their hearts to his preaching even after listening to it and understanding it will find the law of God become a barrier between them and their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the opening address is general, it indirectly warns the weak believers without humiliating them, gives them a chance to reform, and helps the good improve their knowledge and deeds.
rows.anchor: such elements are warned in an indirect way so that they are not humiliated and also they are provided with an opportunity to mend their ways.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying God and the Messenger here means the fullest obedience entailed by faith.
rows.anchor: The verb “obey” is used in the verse in its ultimate sense. The actual meaning would be that believers should obey God and His prophet in the most befitting way that is entailed by their faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about listening underscores the gravity of evading a Messenger one has heard; such a person has no excuse for falling short.
rows.anchor: The words “when you are listening” in “and do not evade their call when you are listening” point to the grave nature of their attitude.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun for the call refers to the Messenger; evading him is evading God, since he is the means to connect with and obey God.
rows.anchor: It is evident from this that evading the Messenger is tantamount to evading God: the only means to connect with God and to obey Him is through His messenger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim to have listened but not to obey recalls the Jews of 2:93, who said they listened and obeyed while acting otherwise, including in the Prophet's presence.
rows.anchor: that this attitude was in the presence of the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocritical Muslims are told that their conduct resembles the Jews and conflicts with obedience to the Messenger; professing faith means not following this condemned nation's way.
rows.anchor: it is insinuated to these hypocritical Muslims that this behaviour they have adopted is not in consonance with obeying the Messenger; it is akin to obeying the Jews.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who hear the Prophet but neither understand nor follow his words are the worst of animals in God's sight.
rows.anchor: if even after hearing they do not listen or use their intellect and also do not follow what the Prophet (sws) says,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who hear the Prophet yet fail to listen, think, or follow him are, in God's sight, the worst of animals.
rows.anchor: then in the sight of God they are the worst of animals.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an elsewhere calls idolaters, Jews, and Christians the worst of animals because they refused to listen and understand; those who follow their way join them.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ān has called Idolaters as well as the Jews and the Christians as the worst of animals because they had refused to listen and understand.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intellect distinguishes humans: without it a person becomes worse than an instinct-following animal, while insight can raise a person to the highest summits and its loss plunges him into the deepest pits.
rows.anchor: the real distinguishing feature of a human being is his faculty of intellect. Without it, he becomes a two legged beast and that too the worst.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people the urge to listen when He finds good in them; this answers why He does not simply force open the minds and hearts of those who reject intellect.
rows.anchor: had He found this ability in them, He would definitely have provided them the urge to understand.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice grants everyone the capacity to distinguish good from evil; using it brings further guidance and growth, while wasting it causes existing guidance to be taken away.
rows.anchor: He has provided every person the ability to distinguish good from evil. Those who keep this ability intact and use it are guided further

rows.speaker: Jesus (sws)
rows.claim: Jesus illustrates that a master would not entrust a thousand coins to a slave who proved dishonest with one coin.
rows.anchor: Jesus (sws) while referring to this fact has very subtly said: Why would a master trust a slave with a thousand coins if he has proven dishonest in one coin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance imposed without receptive ability would be rejected, like food by a failed stomach or seed in barren soil; virtue develops only where human nature can nourish it.
rows.anchor: if God had injected guidance in them without this ability, their natures would have repelled it and it would not have found roots in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if God plants virtue in a person, His law is that it will not develop in a corrupted nature; the seed grows only in upright human nature.
rows.anchor: seed of virtue and vice. It develops according to its potentials only in those human natures which are upright.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life offered by God's call is spiritual life: accepting truth grants insight and intellect, and revives the heart; refusal leaves disbelievers dead with respect to their purpose of creation.
rows.anchor: real life is the life of his heart and his soul. If he loses the ability to contemplate the truth and refuses to accept it, he is actually dead with respect to his purpose of creation.

rows.speaker: Jesus
rows.claim: Jesus is quoted as teaching that human beings live not on bread alone but on every word from God.
rows.anchor: Jesus is reported to have said: “Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.”

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being a barrier between a person and his heart means that God's law and practice become the barrier; effects caused by that law are attributed to God.
rows.anchor: God becoming a barrier here means God’s law become a barrier. At times, things that happen because of God’s law and practice are ascribed to God Himself.

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person can turn back from vice up to a limit, but beyond it the heart becomes uncontrollable; turning from a Messenger's powerful call brings the law that seals hearts into effect.
rows.anchor: When a person starts to indulge in vices, then until a certain limit he can still turn back if he pays heed; however, when this limit is crossed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak and hypocritical Muslims still have time to reform; otherwise their hearts will be sealed and tarnished beyond recovery, and they must consider their coming judgment before God.
rows.anchor: they still have the time to mend their ways. Otherwise, their hearts will be sealed. They will be tarnished to such an extent that it they will never be able to regain their lustre.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses society broadly, especially people focused only on their own reform; they must oppose social evils because a vice that becomes endemic harms silent bystanders as well as its perpetrators.
rows.anchor: if some evil deed becomes rampant in a society, it becomes an endemic. In such a case, its evil effects are not merely to confined to its perpetrators; they also engulf those who remained silent and indifferent to it.

rows.speaker: The Prophet (sws)
rows.claim: The Prophet's ship parable says that if those on deck ignore people below drilling for water, the ship will sink and all aboard will suffer.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) has explained this fact through the parable of the travellers of a ship

rows.speaker: The Prophet
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that one should stop evil by hand, then by tongue if unable, and otherwise reject it in the heart, the lowest level of faith (Muslim 1:69, no. 49).
rows.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said: “When any person among you sees an evil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group that professes truth but cannot meet its demands is warned that failure to reform will let God's law become a barrier between them and their hearts.
rows.anchor: if they do not mend their affairs, the law of God becomes a barrier between them and their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who accept truth without enough commitment to bear others' anger face the social evil's consequences; protection belongs to those who keep enjoining right regardless of people's response.
rows.anchor: Only they will remain protected who will continue to enjoin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's retribution follows an impartial, relentless moral law like physical laws; unchecked exposure to polluted air or bad company similarly affects people.
rows.anchor: the unbiased and relentless nature of the law of retribution. In other words, just as the laws of God are relentless in the physical realm, they are inexorable in the moral realm too.
